To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the jets of XTE J19008+094 are resolved, and expand asymmetrically, as a consequence of the jets impacting the surrounding medium.

(1) the 2013 radio flare from the black hole candidate source XTE J19008+094 was produced by a jet interaction with the surrounding medium, (2) this interaction is asymmetric and complex, and (3) the surrounding medium is denser than previously thought.
we detect moving jet components that expand and evolve in brightness and morphology, and that we infer that the surrounding medium is denser than previously assumed.

the study of the evolution of jets in the black hole X-ray binary system, XTE J1900+094, using very long baseline interferometry.
the study of the structure and dynamics of the jets in XTE J1900+094.
the physics of jets and the accretion processes that drive them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the radio emission is produced by the interaction of the jet with the surrounding medium, and that the radio knots are produced by the jet impacting the medium, with the radio emission produced by synchrotron radiation from the shocked jet plasma.
the observed behaviour of XTE J19008+094 is consistent with that of a jet impacting a dense medium, and is unlike any other jet behaviour seen in any other source.
the jets of XTE J1909+090 are resolved and expanding, and that the knots are working surfaces where the jet is impacting a denser medium than has been inferred for microquasars in the past.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the outburst of XTE J19008+094 is a good example of the complex and dynamic nature of the jets of black hole X-ray binary sources, and the importance of the environment for jet formation and dynamics.
we have observed a new type of transient radio source, which is a black hole X-ray binary that has undergone a state transition and has a resolved expanding radio jet.
XTE J1909+094 is a new type of black hole X-ray binary system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the jet launching mechanism and the environment in which it operates can change on a timescale of days, and that this can be probed by high angular resolution radio imaging.
the jets of this black hole system are not steady, but rather expand laterally as they travel, and that the expansion rate is faster than previously observed in black hole systems.
the jets from black hole X-ray binaries can be complex, and that they can interact with the environment on a timescale of days.
